name: mcp-books
description: MCP server that searches the Internet Archive, the Library of Congress and data.bnf.fr at once, inside scanned text and across catalogues. No API key required.
long_description:
Ask where a phrase was ever printed, or what a catalogue holds under a title, and several archives answer at once: the Internet Archive, holding the machine-read text of digitised books, periodicals and documents; the Library of Congress, holding the text of American newspaper pages; and data.bnf.fr, the open catalogue of the Bibliothèque nationale de France, which describes works as entities rather than copies. The corpora are different bodies of material, so the answer is those put together rather than one question asked several times.

What makes the merge usable is what it refuses to flatten. A page number is a real leaf on an archive whose index holds one and null on an archive whose index holds none, and no page is ever invented. An excerpt says what it is: the passage that matched, or the opening of a page sent because the searched words sit further down than the text that came back. Counts are reported in each archive's own terms and never added. The fields each catalogue searched are published, because the same words put to an index over a whole record and to an index over titles alone are two questions. A narrowing an archive cannot apply is never sent to it, and the answer names it. Terms of reuse are stated per record, and an archive publishing on a condition carries that condition and the date its metadata was retrieved.

An archive that fails is named, with the moment that failed. An archive that cannot answer a question is named as absent, with the reason, rather than quietly left out.
